updates.name: Cayelan C. Carey
updates.bio: Professor of freshwater ecosystem science in Virginia Tech's Department of Biological Sciences, leading a lab that pairs high-frequency lake and reservoir sensor data with ecosystem models to issue near-term water-quality forecasts, with emphasis on algal blooms and hypoxia. Co-directs Virginia Tech's Center for Ecosystem Forecasting and founded Macrosystems EDDIE, an undergraduate data-science teaching program.
updates.research_interests: near-term freshwater ecological forecasting; nutrient and carbon cycling in lakes and reservoirs; feedbacks between aquatic biogeochemistry and plankton food webs; management of hypoxia and algal blooms; reservoir greenhouse gas dynamics; environmental data science education

updates.name: Charles A. Stock
updates.bio: Research oceanographer at NOAA's Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory in Princeton, trained at Princeton, Stanford and the MIT/WHOI Joint Program. Develops marine ecosystem and biogeochemistry components for GFDL's Earth system model and applies GFDL models to project climate effects on ocean ecosystems over seasons to decades. Has co-led NOAA's national modeling team for the Climate, Ecosystems and Fisheries Initiative.
updates.research_interests: global and regional marine ecosystem and biogeochemical dynamics; climate change impacts on marine ecosystems; climate downscaling; sub-seasonal to decadal ecological prediction; marine resource dynamics and management

updates.name: Christopher A. Scholin
updates.bio: Senior scientist at the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute, which he headed as president and CEO from 2009 until 2026. updates.name: Christopher J. McNeil
updates.bio: Geophysicist at the USGS Alaska Science Center in Anchorage. Studies basin- to regional-scale changes in glacier area, volume and mass and their consequences for local ecosystems and sea level, including reanalysis of the long USGS benchmark glacier records, drawing on field measurements, historical aerial and commercial satellite imagery, and high-performance computing.
updates.research_interests: glacier area, volume and mass change; reanalysis and homogenization of USGS benchmark glacier records; drivers of glacier change (hypsometry, snow accumulation, energy balance, ice dynamics); glacier impacts on ecosystems and sea level; geodesy and remote sensing
updates.current_affiliation: U.S. Geological Survey, Alaska Science Center

updates.name: Christopher L. Sabine
updates.bio: Professor in the University of Hawaii at Manoa Department of Oceanography, in its Marine Geology and Geochemistry group.
